clue.text: Made neat, because tangled

parts.note: for in the sense 'since, because' (as in 'for it was late')
matted hair is tangled and knotted

explanation.surface: Someone explains why hair or a document was tidied: because it was in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Formatted text has been laid out and arranged, so it has been made neat and orderly.

clue.text: Four regularly on watch, or part of it

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the next comes before it
taking letters at regular intervals from the word Four, here the first and third

parts.note: to watch is to see

explanation.surface: Four people take turns on watch, or perhaps only some of them do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'watch': the definition is a part of a watch, not a sentry's watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusee is the cone-shaped grooved pulley in a mechanical timepiece that evens out the spring's pull.

clue.text: Traditional meal of boar's feet prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rustic dish of pig's trotters, cooked the old way.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is the classic British Sunday dinner, a long-established national dish.

clue.text: Look — seed inside a caper

indicators.note: the seed word sits within the letters of 'a caper'

parts.note: to caper is to prance about
a pea is a seed from a pod

explanation.surface: Someone points out a seed in a caper, the pickled bud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caper' looks like the pickled bud but is the verb, to skip about.
explanation.definitionFit: Appearance and look are synonyms for how someone or something seems outwardly.

clue.text: Meal includes stewed rump and fried seafood

indicators.note: the meal word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in parts of Britain

indicators.note: stewed meat is cooked down and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A menu offering a dinner of stewed rump steak with some fried fish alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal' looks like the definition, but the Japanese dish at the end is the answer; 'stewed' scrambles the rump.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is the Japanese dish of shellfish or vegetables dipped in light batter and deep-fried.

clue.text: Drop mark, having cheated to secure it

indicators.note: the cheating word grips the mark word, holding it inside

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: An exam candidate loses a mark after being caught cheating to get it.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to throw it away or drop it.

clue.text: I take off Bohemian clothing (only a bit)

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème, a Bohemian in Paris

indicators.note: just a small part of the word clothing is used, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone strips off clothes in Bohemian style, though only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: an impressionist could say 'I take off', meaning I imitate people.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to imitate them, which is what an impressionist does for a living.

clue.text: Finally acclaim own Scottish chief

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word acclaim is used

parts.note: ain is the Scots form of own, as in 'my ain folk'

explanation.surface: At last a Scottish clan chief of one's own is hailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Main and chief are synonyms meaning principal or most important.

clue.text: Intelligent group of people endlessly miserable

parts.note: men are people

indicators.note: the word for miserable loses its final letter

parts.note: sad means miserable

explanation.surface: Clever people who are perpetually gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is the society whose members must score highly on an IQ test.

clue.text: As writer, Shakespeare's surely holding leading place

indicators.note: the archaic word for surely wraps around the other piece

parts.note: certes is an archaic word for certainly, used by Shakespeare
the van, short for vanguard, is the front position

explanation.surface: As a writer, Shakespeare surely holds the top spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare is a red herring for the writer: he only supplies an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes was the Spanish author of Don Quixote, a novelist and playwright.

clue.text: Rascal's party succeeded at first

indicators.note: the abbreviation for succeeded is placed at the start, before the party word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
a camp is a group or faction holding a view

explanation.surface: A rogue's political party won at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous young rogue, a rascal.

clue.text: Evangelist who spends little touring holy city

indicators.note: the tight-fisted word goes round the city word, enclosing it

parts.note: a miser hoards money and spends little
Sion, or Zion, is Jerusalem, the holy city

explanation.surface: A thrifty preacher travels around Jerusalem on the cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: A missioner is a missionary, someone who goes out to spread the gospel.

clue.text: Additional artwork not done on campus

parts.note: extra means additional
a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: An extra piece of art that wasn't made at the university.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramural study or work takes place outside a university's walls, beyond the main institution.

clue.text: Language OK for Willi and Virginia

parts.note: ja is German for yes, what a German called Willi would say
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A German and a woman named Virginia both approve of a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is a widely used programming language, also the Indonesian island's name.

clue.text: Moving house?

parts.note: read not as relocating but as a dwelling that itself moves, a caravan-style home on wheels

explanation.surface: A question about relocating to a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving house' normally means changing address; here it describes a house that moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile home is a large caravan or prefabricated dwelling that can be towed from site to site.

clue.text: Music man roused at 7

indicators.note: stirred up and agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 7-down, the high-IQ society

explanation.surface: A musician gets excited about joining a society of clever people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roused' shuffles the letters of the 7-down answer with AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer, best known for Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Farm animals we hear in city

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken and the answer only sounds like it

parts.note: a farm is the home of livestock, or stock, so read as 'stock home'

explanation.surface: Livestock can be heard in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: A farm is where stock live: a 'stock home', which said out loud is close to the Swedish capital's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockholm is the capital of Sweden, a city built across islands.

clue.text: Endlessly valiant, securing water at last in this?

definitions.text: Endlessly valiant, securing water at last in this?

indicators.note: the shortened brave word holds the other letter inside it
the word for valiant loses its final letter

parts.note: doughty means brave or valiant

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word water is used

explanation.surface: Bravely enduring until water finally arrives during a long dry spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts DOUGHTY to DOUGHT, and R goes inside it; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long period without rain, when people must be valiant until water comes at last.

clue.text: Many died here of French disease, losing both feet

indicators.note: each of the two words drops its foot, the bottom letter in a down clue

parts.note: Gallic means French, from Gaul
polio is a viral disease

explanation.surface: A battlefield where many soldiers died of a French disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing both feet' trims the last letter of each piece, C and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the 1915-16 First World War campaign in Turkey with huge casualties on both sides.

clue.text: Policeman belonging to Brazilian port shortly returns

parts.note: of means belonging to, as in 'friend of mine'

indicators.note: the shortened port name is read backwards
the port's name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Recife is a port city in north-east Brazil

explanation.surface: A police officer from a Brazilian port comes back briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts RECIFE to RECIF and 'returns' reads it backwards as FICER.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is the general term for a member of the police force.

clue.text: Service concerning peace, short mass

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the word for peace is cut, dropping its final letter

parts.note: quiet is peace
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A brief church service of mass, about peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like part of the church scene but is just the physics abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A requiem is a Mass or church service held for the dead.

clue.text: Clamps down on crossing points: fine to go through

indicators.note: the fine letter passes into the middle of the crossing word

parts.note: stiles are steps for crossing a fence or wall
F is the abbreviation for fine, on pencils

explanation.surface: Authorities crack down at border crossings, letting penalties pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle something is to suppress or restrain it, to clamp down on it.

clue.text: Peace soon around new airport

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the word for soon goes round the abbreviation for new

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: Calm will soon return to a newly built airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Shannon is an international airport in the west of Ireland, once a transatlantic refuelling stop.

clue.text: Give up excitement

definitions.meaning: to stop a habit, as in quitting smoking
a thrill, as in doing something just for the buzz

explanation.surface: Abandoning the thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: Kick means both to give up a habit and a thrill or buzz.

clue.text: Ball lands in short playing area

indicators.note: the ball letter drops into the middle of the other word

parts.note: curt means short or brusque
O is round, like a ball

explanation.surface: A tennis ball lands just inside the line in a short playing area.
explanation.definitionFit: A court is a marked area for games like tennis, squash or basketball.

clue.text: City to look cheerful as soldiers enter

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the cheerful word

parts.note: to smile is to look happy
qua is Latin for in the capacity of, as
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A town brightens up when the army marches in.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's financial district is nicknamed the Square Mile.
explanation.definitionFit: The City, capital C, is London's financial district, about a mile square.

clue.text: Rugby game doesn't start with equal chances

indicators.note: the rugby word loses its opening letter

parts.note: sevens is a seven-a-side form of rugby union

explanation.surface: A rugby match is delayed, so the odds are even.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens are betting odds of one to one, an equal chance of winning or losing.

clue.text: Cautious movement of ship over river

indicators.note: the ship word lies over the river letter, covering it on both sides

parts.note: way is a ship's progress through water, as in 'making way'

explanation.surface: A careful ship crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Wary means watchful and careful of danger, so cautious.

clue.text: Enthusiastic reception welcoming outwardly usual monthly event

indicators.note: the applause word takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: an ovation is enthusiastic applause

indicators.note: only the outer letters of usual, first and last, are used

explanation.surface: Applause greets something that happens regularly every month.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovulation, release of an egg from the ovary, happens roughly once a month.

clue.text: Gas, about 28 gm?

parts.note: an ounce is roughly 28 grams, so the weight reads as '...', run together as a word for a gas

explanation.surface: A question about how much a small amount of gas weighs.
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce is about 28 grams: written as 'oz one', it spells the gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen, a pungent gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Walter, a handyman?

definitions.meaning: Walter of the Thurber story, the daydreamer of 'The Secret Life'
playfully, someone who is all mitts, mitt being slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A man called Walter who may be good with tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Mitty is James Thurber's fantasist; mitt-y jokingly suggests full of hands.

clue.text: Mushroom that is consumed in minutes, seasonal speciality

indicators.note: the pieces are swallowed up inside the minutes word

parts.note: mins is short for minutes
a cep is a wild mushroom, the porcino
ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A mushroom eaten in minutes as a festive treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince pies are small sweet pastries filled with dried fruit, eaten at Christmas.
